findings.where: Traces, every screen: the dashed '440 V' line
findings.what: Each trace is one coil, so one phase, but its peak is drawn on a line labelled 440 V, which is the set's line-to-line RMS; a 440 V set's phase actually peaks at about 359 V (440 ÷ √3 × √2), so label the line 'full field' (or draw the phase peak) and make the Voltage tile say it is between lines.

'Speeding up raises the voltage a little too. The field current can then trim that back' contradicts the screen's own Check, which takes 1740 rev/min, 58 Hz, 425 V to 1800 rev/min, 60 Hz, 440 V with the field unchanged, so there is nothing to trim; say the voltage comes back with the speed.

The Pole pairs tile reads 2 before Check because hide lists only f and V, so the screen hands over the poles-or-pole-pairs step that both its slips (120 Hz, 30 Hz) exist to catch; hide 'pp' as screens 11 and 12 do.

The brief promised a recall opener (AC circuits lesson 1's coil spun twice as fast: taller and shorter waves together, 'Still there') and the lesson has none, though the Transformers lessons carry theirs; it would also set up screen 9's point that speed moves frequency and voltage together.

With 4 poles the coils sit 60° apart round the stator, but the text only says a set of three per pole pair 'keeps the three phases 120° apart in the wave'; one sentence closes the step: a pole pair passes in half a turn, so a third of that is 60° of rotor and 120° of wave.

findings.where: Screen 6 (Cycles in a turn), picture and tiles
findings.what: The question is about a 6-pole rotor, yet until Check the picture is a 4-pole rotor and the tiles read Pole pairs 2, 1800 rev/min, 60 Hz and 440 V, a different machine; hide the tiles until Check so nothing on screen argues with the question.
The screen opens already on 4 poles, so 'Switch the rotor to 4 poles' asks for a move that has been made; 'Now the rotor has 4 poles' reads true.

Every pole setting is a 60 Hz machine, so the Voltage tile reads 367 V for the 2-pole set at 3000 rev/min (before Check) and for the 6-pole set at 1000 rev/min making 50 Hz (after Check), which will puzzle him; hide Voltage on those two screens.

The glow follows the coil's voltage, so it is brightest when the gap between poles faces the coil and dark with a pole square in front, but no sentence says so and the picture's description says a coil 'glows while a pole passes it'; one line (a coil lights while its flux changes fastest, between poles) would make the glow a proof of screen 2.

'A click is the same size at any speed' is not true of a magnetic pickup, the usual sensor on a diesel's flywheel teeth, whose pulses grow with speed just as the coil's voltage does; say a count is a count whatever its size, or name a Hall-effect or optical sensor.

It says the alternator is the turning-coil generator 'turned inside out' but never says why; the brief asked for one plain line given as reasoning (the big output currents leave through fixed connections, and only the small field current crosses onto the rotor).
Both multiple-choice puzzles put the right answer first; vary the order so the position never hints.

'It asks what each one does when two sets share one board' has no clear 'it'; and footnote [^3] sits on a plain statement ('its field turns with it') rather than a value he would look up, while [^2] sits inside the bold summary.
The rotor turns only by dragging its ring: the Rotor position control (#c-turn) is always hidden, so there is no keyboard way to turn it.
